overview: The Wausau Police & Fire Commission held a brief public meeting that drew significant public comment focused on the city's Flock license plate reader camera system, with three residents raising privacy and oversight concerns. The commission then approved minutes from the prior meeting and moved into closed session to interview candidates for firefighter/paramedic and police detective positions, as well as to consider a citizen complaint reconsideration request.
presiding: Chair name not stated in transcript

Closed Session – Interviews of Two Candidates for Firefighter/Paramedic and One Candidate for Promotion to Detective
Closed Session – Reconsideration Request of Dismissal of Citizen Complaint of JV

discussions.item: Public Comment – Flock License Plate Reader System
discussions.body: Three residents spoke during public comment, all raising concerns about the Flock automated license plate reader (ALPR) system. Felix Gallow of 1206 Highland Park Boulevard presented data alleging widespread surveillance abuse and called on the commission to close data sharing with outside agencies, limit search access to supervisors, require case IDs for every search, and overhaul the audit process. Courtney Olsen, also of 1206 Highland Park Boulevard, identified herself as a domestic violence advocate and police trainer, asking the commission to use its oversight role to request a report on arrests and convictions tied to Flock data, an audit of outside-agency searches, and the department's own camera location list before the city council votes on the $50,000 budget item. Mary CL of 127 Kent Street spoke as a concerned neighbor, citing personal experience with a stalker and expressing discomfort with private companies collecting movement data on residents without clear data security guarantees. The chair acknowledged the comments and noted the topic would be discussed during adjournment.

discussions.item: Consideration of Minutes from Preceding Meeting
discussions.body: A commissioner requested a clarification on page five of the minutes regarding a fire/EMS audit reference to two agencies listed as 'USDA' and 'DEA,' asking which agency conducted the audit and that acronyms be spelled out. The chair confirmed the audit was conducted by the U.S. Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA) and directed that correction be made. The minutes were then approved with that correction on a voice vote.

The commission voted to enter closed session under Wisconsin State Statute 19.85(1)(c) to interview two candidates for firefighter/paramedic with the Wausau Fire Department and one candidate for promotion to detective with the Wausau Police Department, and under 19.85(1)(f) to consider a reconsideration request regarding the dismissal of a citizen complaint identified as JV. The motion passed on a voice vote.

publicComment: Three speakers addressed the commission, all on the topic of the Flock license plate reader system. Felix Gallow (1206 Highland Park Blvd.) cited research on surveillance abuse and made four specific policy recommendations. Courtney Olsen (1206 Highland Park Blvd.), a domestic violence advocate and police trainer, asked the commission to request accountability data from the police department before budget decisions are finalized. Mary CL (127 Kent Street) spoke as a private citizen concerned about privacy, data security, and the potential for stalkers or other bad actors to access Flock data.
